answer.rationale: Incumbent refuses to reopen price, finance demands 18% cut, contract expires in 14 days with no auto-renew, and line is at 94% of committed volume with no buffer. Forcing renegotiation fails (memory_c4 needs a willing counterparty and benchmarking against market; here the incumbent has refused). Renewing (memory_c1) preserves stability but will not meet the 18% cut, and at this volume with no buffer the service scope may already be eroding. Memory_c2 indicates the low-cost vendor delivered a sharp unit-cost reduction with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing last year; combined with memory_c3, a parallel second source is the right hedge during a constrained window. I will verify memory_c2 to confirm the onboarding speed and invoicing accuracy claim before committing, since execution speed is the limiting factor with 14 days to expiry and no buffer. The action is to issue a small, time-boxed purchase order to the low-cost vendor for the constrained component (or for a non-critical slice of primary supply) to validate price, lead time, and delivery reliability before the contract expires, while keeping the incumbent on month-to-month (memory_c5 pattern) until the test returns. If the test confirms, expand to full primary switch; if it fails, fall back to renewal. This avoids increasing delivery risk because the line stays on the incumbent's proven volume until the new vendor's performance is proven on real orders, and it positions us to hit the 18% spend reduction without re-opening a closed negotiation.
